overview: 오늘 조합은 전반적 위험선호가 강하지도, 전면적 위험회피로 기울지도 않은 ‘선별적 디레버리징과 관망’의 그림에 가깝다: 위험자산 중에서도 성장·모멘텀 축이 상대적으로 약세 신호를 유지하는 반면(동일 범주의 다른 구성원은 중립), 안전자산은 최근의 약세 국면에서 벗어나 일단 안정(중립)으로 돌아섰지만 강한 방어 캐시는 보이지 않는다(달러 역시 중립). 인플레이션·공급 헤지 축에서는 금과 산업금속이 동반 약세 신호인 가운데, 에너지와 광범위 원자재는 며칠 전 동조 매수 전환 시도가 짧게 끝나며 다시 중립으로 식어 물가 압력 재가열의 일관된 흐름은 약하다. 최근 이력상 10/06의 주식 동시 매수 전환과 10/16의 원자재 측 동조화가 모두 빠르게 되돌려진 점은 오늘의 혼조·분산 상태를 강화한다. 눈에 띄는 괴리는 동일 자산군 내 스타일/구성 간 분화(주식에서 성장 대비 광범위지수의 버팀, 크립토에서 이더 약세 속 비트코인 중립)와 금·산업금속의 동반 약세 대비 에너지의 중립적 버팀으로, 이는 광범위한 리스크오프보다는 선택적 위험 축소와 방향성 부재가 지배적이라는 신호로 해석된다.

news.title: Last week saw the largest tech sell skew in more than 5 years, says Jefferies
news.summary:
- Jefferies reports last week’s tech trading was the most selling-tilted in over five years, driven by broad market angst and de-grossing flows, with a net $7.5B of tech selling by Friday.
- Concentrated weakness in semiconductors, memory, hardware, and communications equipment; software/IT services saw more buying on the week.
- The Nasdaq Composite fell ~3%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped about 10%.
- Key concerns: tightening/volatile credit and funding for AI-related capex, including stress around CoreWeave (backed by Nvidia) and imperfect access to cheaper capital amid macro headwinds (Iran conflict, US debt, trade tensions).
- The AI/tech rally may be cooling despite still-strong demand signals in semiconductors, with QQQ components trading at the cheapest forward P/E in ~6 years.
- Outlook take: near-term weakness persisted, but indicators show stabilization in positioning and ongoing long-term demand in semis; stronger catalysts needed to reverse momentum.

news.title: Nasdaq 100 Forecast: Chip Selloff Tests Uptrend After Record High | FXEmpire
news.summary:
Summary:
- The Nasdaq 100 has pulled back from a record high as semiconductor equities weaken, pressured by competition from Chinese chipmakers and AI funding concerns. The index sits around 29,213 after failing to hold 30,600, with a need to reclaim 29,900 to target higher levels toward 30,600.
- Positive chip earnings from ASML and TSMC (record/strong revenue outlook) support ongoing chip demand, yet doubts remain about whether AI investments will translate into profits high enough to justify infrastructure costs.
- Technically, the breakout signals weakened: an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern failed above 30,600, and the chart shows a descending broadening wedge. The Nasdaq remains above key moving averages (50- and 200-week SMAs), but the near-term outlook is cautious until the index stabilizes above 29,900.
- Key near-term catalysts: Meta’s and other AI-related earnings (with Nvidia-like expectations around AI spending) and any updates on AI funding/ profitability. A stronger AI spending outlook could bolster sentiment, while funding concerns continue to cap gains.

User-focused angle:
- If you’re assessing Nasdaq tech stock prospects, the path forward hinges on stabilizing above 29,900 and confirming chip demand can sustain profitable AI infrastructure spending. Positive chip results are a tailwind, but funding and margins remain critical headwinds.

news.title: The AI Rubber Band Snaps Back | Investing.com
news.summary:
Summary:
The article argues that while AI-related equities saw a Monday rally, the move was more a short-covering rebound than a durable revival. Key points: the SOX and Nasdaq 100 edged up, but AI demand financing remains questionable as credit spreads widen and safe-haven demand unwinds; yields rise and the dollar/gold/bitcoin soften, signaling a risk reset rather than a full risk-on shift. Oil staying above $100 keeps inflation risks alive and limits near-term Fed tightening upside. Earnings-driven moves are increasingly about guidance and future capex profitability, not just current results. The market remains focused on who pays for ongoing compute spend, at what cost of capital, and whether hyperscalers can sustain investment without deteriorating returns. Overall, a cautious tone: sentiment improved modestly, but financing constraints and higher yields pose ongoing hurdles for a durable tech/AI rally.

news.title: Nasdaq 100 Sees Best Day In Nearly A Month As AI Rout Cools — AMZN, BE, CRWV, AAPL, PLTR In Focus
news.summary:
Summary:
- The Nasdaq 100 posted its best day in nearly a month, up about 1.2% as AI-related stocks rebounded after a recent rout.
- S&P 500 rose 0.4%, while Dow fell 0.1%; Nasdaq-100 futures and broader tech ETFs saw gains, with QQQ up 1.2% and semis (SMH, SOX) rallying around 1.6–2%.
- Key drivers: renewed interest in AI plays (NVDA, MU, AVGO among movers); concerns persisted from AI market headwinds (Anthropic’s reported sales, Gartner capex warn) and CoreWeave credit stress.
- Market sentiment improved for QQQ but remained cautious for broader equities. Traders eye upcoming earnings from Meta (META) and Tesla (TSLA) for growth signals.
- Notable stock moves: Amazon (AMZN) near three-month high on optimistic Morgan Stanley note; Apple (AAPL) confirmed a major product launch event (Oct 28); BE and PLTR rose on related developments (data center/defense deployment initiatives).

Bottom line for Nasdaq tech stock outlook:
- Short-term: AI stock rally appears resumed but fragile; semis-led strength suggests continued volatility tied to AI capex and earnings guidance.
- Medium term: Watch META and TSLA earnings for broader AI-growth validation; sector rotation may hinge on profitability versus hype in AI infrastructure names.

news.title: Is this the beginning of the end of the AI stock market boom?
news.summary:
Title: Is this the beginning of the end of the AI stock market boom? | The Guardian

Summary:
- The Guardian weighs whether this year’s roughly $1 trillion AI investment is overhyped, noting a 5.5% drop in the Nasdaq 100 and renewed anxiety about an AI stock market bust.
- Some see a valuation reset rather than a fundamental AI failure. The Nasdaq 100 remains substantially higher than early 2023, and the “magnificent seven” (Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla) dominate a larger share of the S&P 500.
- Risks highlighted:
  - Open-source AI could undermine ROI from big bets, potentially deflating valuations.
  - Political and social opposition to AI infrastructure (e.g., data centers) and potential worker impacts.
  - Rising debt and heavy AI-related capital expenditure by hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Apple) increasing exposure to credit markets.
- Earnings season ahead will test whether lofty AI valuations are justified; some analysts view the pullback as profit-taking rather than a rejection of AI’s long-term potential.
- Historically, tech booms have overbuilt capacity, suggesting a more balanced, albeit cautious, reassessment rather than a collapse.

Why it matters for Nasdaq tech stock outlook:
- Short-term volatility amid a broader market valuation reset, with questions about the pace and sustainability of AI-driven returns.
- Structural trend toward AI remains, but investors are cautious about debt levels, open-source competition, and regulatory/social risks.

news.title: Ether Struggles as Inflation Fears Grow and Investors Withdraw Money | FXEmpire
news.summary:
Ethereum price outlook analysis:

- Ether faces two headwinds: rising US inflation and potential rate hikes, which reduce appetite for risk assets, and ongoing net withdrawals from ether ETFs, led by BlackRock’s ETHA, signaling weaker near-term demand.
- The Glamsterdam network upgrade could improve efficiency but does not guarantee a higher Ether price or reversal in inflation/interest-rate concerns.
- Current price context: Ethereum trades around the mid-2,400s after a pullback from a recent $2,800 resistance, with near-term focus on the Fed decision (Oct 28) and ETF flow data.
- Key takeaway: Upgrades may boost network performance, but macro factors (inflation, rates) and investor demand remain decisive for Ether’s price trajectory. Positive price action would likely require a shift in demand, not just tech improvements.

news.title: Ethereum consolidates around key technical levels amid a challenging macro backdrop. What to watch next?
news.summary:

The near-term focus is Friday’s US Flash PMIs; weak data could spark another ETH selloff, while surprisingly strong data may prompt a short-term relief rally without changing the longer-term rate-hike outlook. Technical view:
- Daily: ETH holding around 2,360 support and an upward trendline; risk to the downside below the trendline toward 1,900; upside target around 3,400.
- 4-hour: Bearish trendline with selling pressure; a break above the trendline could bolster a move toward 2,570 as a near-term target.

news.title: Ethereum Price Forecast as JPMorgan Brings JPM Coin to the Network
news.summary:
Ethereum price outlook analysis:

- Price action: ETH is edging higher, up 1.16% to around $2,407, and holding above $2,390 as the broader market gains. The near-term target remains up to $2,500, with bearish pressure fading but not yet gone.

- Key catalyst: JPMorgan’s JPM Coin launch on Ethereum mainnet expands institutional payment capabilities (tokenized dollar deposits settled 24/7). This development could strengthen Ethereum’s role as a settlement layer for tokenized assets and digital money, supporting demand from institutions.

- Technical view: A potential long-side breakout would require a sustained four-hour close above $2,400 to open the path to $2,500 and potentially toward $2,600 if momentum continues. Support sits near $2,330, with a psychological level around $2,300 in play if the floor gives way. Current RSI ~46 and MACD readings suggest bearish pressure is easing but no definitive bullish cross yet.

-  ETF flow context: Ethereum ETFs saw net outflows of about $69.68 million (Oct 16), led by BlackRock’s ETHA, though overall market cap exposure remains significant.

- Near-term uncertainty: Fed rate decision could introduce volatility, so momentum may hinge on macro triggers alongside the JPM Coin integration.

Bottom line: The outlook favors a bullish tilt toward $2,500 if ETH can sustain above $2,400 on a four-hour basis, aided by increased institutional adoption via JPM Coin on the Ethereum network. Failure to hold $2,330 could reintroduce downside risk toward $2,300.

news.title: CIO remains constructive on gold over the next 12 months | UBS United States
news.summary:
Summary:
UBS CIO remains constructive on gold over the next 12 months despite near-term headwinds from higher real yields and a firm US dollar. Key macro drivers supporting gold’s role as a strategic hedge include robust central bank demand and reserve diversification, elevated government debt, and geopolitical uncertainty. UBS forecasts gold rising toward about USD 5,400/oz by September 2027, with pullbacks toward USD 4,000/oz seen as opportunities to add exposure. For now, a mid-single-digit allocation to gold is suggested for those inclined, with more diversification into other commodities for larger holdings. Near-term volatility is expected from rising yields and dollar strength, but fundamental demand themes may keep gold resilient as a store of value and portfolio diversifier.

news.title: CIBC slashes gold price forecasts but sees recovery to $5,200 in 2027 as central bank demand offsets Fed headwinds | Kitco News
news.summary:
Summary: CIBC Capital Markets lowers near-term gold forecasts but remains constructive longer term, forecasting prices average about $4,500 in Q4 2026 and $5,200 in 2027 (down from prior $6,500 forecasts). The bank trims 2028 to $5,500 and projects 2029–2031 averages around $4,800, $4,500, and $4,200 respectively. Key macro drivers: persistent inflation and geopolitical tensions support gold longer term, while near-term headwinds include higher real interest rates and a stronger dollar, plus Treasury yields above 5%. The outlook notes that if inflation cools and the Fed eases more than expected, real rates could fall below 2%, potentially sparking a recovery. Structural support from investment demand and central bank purchases remains important, with record ETF inflows (Q3) and ongoing central bank diversification away from USD-denominated assets.

Bottom line in the context of the user query (gold price outlook macro drivers): 
- Long-term macro drivers (inflation persistence, geopolitical risk, central bank demand) remain supportive for gold, underpinning the 2027–2029 price path at ~$5k+ averages even as 2026–2028 forecasts are cut. 
- Near-term dynamics (higher real yields, stronger dollar, rising U.S. rates) pose downside risk to gold prices.
- Structural demand (ETFs, central bank purchases) could offset some negative momentum and help price recovery if inflation cools and monetary policy eases.

news.title: Gold Awaits a Range Breakout as Persistent Uncertainty Surrounds FOMC Decision | Investing.com
news.summary:
Gold price outlook: The market is in a defining range ahead of the Fed’s late-October decision. Key macro drivers include:
- Inflation signals: September CPI (3.7% YoY headline, 2.6% core) and PPI (6.3% YoY) underpin expectations for Fed policy and risk sentiment. A potential quarter-point rate hike remained on the table but tempered by Powell’s recent remarks highlighting persistent inflation as a global challenge.
- Fed policy path: Markets anticipate possible near-term rate moves, with guidance from the FOMC meeting emphasis on how inflation evolves and the pace of monetary tightening.
- Technical backdrop: Gold faces resistance near the 20 EMA (~$4,216.93) after a test above the 9 EMA, with all major moving averages below the 200 EMA, indicating a bearish crossover. The price action shows a “Bearish Hammer” and range-bound trading, raising the risk of trap-breakouts at resistance or abrupt reversals at support.
- Seasonal/event risk: The upcoming Fed rate decision (late October) is likely to trigger a decisive directional move, though previous patterns suggest potential continued range-trading until clarity on the policy path emerges.
- Price indicators: Past late-October declines (around 4.5% on similar dates) suggest sensitivity to Fed decisions; watch for a breakout above resistance or a break below support for confirmation of direction.

Bottom line: Near-term momentum is mixed; gold may remain range-bound until the Fed decision provides clearer guidance on the trajectory of policy and inflation pressures. Traders should be cautious of false breakouts and monitor the 20 EMA resistance and the 200 EMA bias, along with evolving inflation data and Fed commentary.

news.title: Gold extends losses as rising Oil prices reinforce Fed rate hike bets
news.summary: Summary: The article notes a near-term rebound in gold (XAU/USD) as oil pulls back on positive Middle East headlines, which also dampens US dollar strength and Treasury yields. Gold trades around $4,143 after an intraday low of $4,111. Oil (WTI) retracted toward $95.65 from above $100, easing energy-driven inflation concerns and contributing to the dollar yield decline. Despite the rebound, upside is capped by lingering geopolitical risks (Saudi Arabia–Houthi tensions; Strait of Hormuz disruptions) that keep supply risks elevated, supporting higher energy costs and inflation pressures. US CPI and PPI data came in hotter-than-expected, keeping the Fed on a cautious path with possible December rate hikes, though traders still price a likely hold at the October meeting (low probability of a near-term cut; ~17% chance of a hike in October, ~92% for December). Technically, XAU/USD remains in a broad range between $4,100 and $4,200, with resistance at $4,200 (and then $4,235 and $4,321) and support near $4,000–$3,950. The price is also constrained by being below the 50-/100-/200-day SMAs, with RSI in the low 40s and a positive MACD signal. Overall macro drivers to watch: USD strength, US yields, oil prices, and Fed expectations, all influencing gold’s safe-haven demand and dollar-denominated pricing.

news.title: XAU/USD Technical & Macro Outlook: October 2026
news.summary:
Gold price outlook macro drivers (XAU/USD) – key takeaways

- Macro drivers: Persistent inflation keeps central banks hawkish (Fed likely to stay “higher for longer” into 2027), with the October–November 2026 CPI readings and major central bank meetings (ECB, BOJ) signaling whether inflation is structural or transitory. Market pricing shows a strong bias toward further Fed tightening or retaining higher rates.

- Gold’s conflicting forces: 
  - Inflation hedge/safe-haven demand supports gold in the near term.
  - Rising U.S. yields and a stronger dollar from ongoing rate hikes increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold, weighing on prices.

- Technical context: XAU/USD may be forming a bullish flag within the long-term uptrend (since 2023), with key support in the 4,000–4,120 region. A breakout above the 4,260–4,408 zone would bolster a resumed rally; a break below 4,000–4,120 could target lower pivots around 3,829.

- Market odds (Fed path): High probability (roughly 83%) of the Fed funds target staying in the 375–400 bps range through the year, with a smaller chance (~17%) of another hike to 400–425 bps, keeping the “higher for longer” stance.

Bottom line: Gold remains in a tug-of-war between sticky inflation risks (supporting demand) and the headwinds from higher real yields and a stronger dollar (pressuring prices). The near-term trajectory hinges on CPI outcomes and Fed policy signals. Technically, a break above the 4,260–4,408 resistance would renew the bullish long-term view, while a break below 4,000–4,120 could open downside levels toward ~3,829.

news.title: Natural Gas Market Indicators – October 16, 2026 - American Gas Association
news.summary:
Summary: Natural Gas Price Outlook Maco Analysis

- Near-term price trend: Henry Hub prompt-month prices have strengthened in October, with the November 2026 contract at $3.24/MMBtu on Oct 15 (up ~7.6% from late Sept), but still below late-September levels and broadly in line with summer pricing. Month-to-date average for November futures through Oct 15 was about $3.15/MMBtu, modestly below June averages.

- Supply picture: U.S. dry gas production remains strong and is on pace for a new annual record, supported by robust supply despite offshore Gulf disruption from Hurricane Isaias. October 16 YTD production is about 4.1% above last year (year-to-date) with October month-to-date about 3.4% higher YoY. U.S. storage inventories sit around 3,567 Bcf (week ending Oct 9), 1.3% above the five-year average, narrowing vs. last week’s 2.0% surplus.

- Demand dynamics: Total U.S. gas demand (including exports) remains strong entering Q4 2026, up over 3% YTD through Oct 16 driven by LNG feedgas and power generation, while domestic residential/commercial demand has softened modestly.

- LNG and international risk: LNG feedgas demand supports domestic price strength; however, ongoing geopolitical tensions and LNG supply disruptions create upside risk to Europe’s gas outlook, potentially influencing global pricing pressures.

- Market sentiment and risk factors:
  - Weather: Six weeks left in the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season; prolonged shut-ins could affect output, though current supply looks resilient.
  - Infrastructure: New pipeline capacity could influence Permian production and regional prices.
  - Storage position: Storage surplus over five-year average narrowed to 1.3%, leaving less cushion as the heating season approaches.

Bottom line: The macro outlook for natural gas prices in the near term remains cushioned by robust U.S. supply and growing LNG demand, with prices plausibly range-bound around the mid-$3/MMBtu area into winter. Risks lean toward upside if LNG demand or European disruption intensifies, or if weather-induced outages reduce U.S. supply.

news.title: Natural gas: Global price convergence delayed until 2028 - Societe General
news.summary:
Summary:
Societe Generale warns that global price convergence for natural gas is expected to be delayed until 2028. The macro outlook suggests prolonged dispersion in regional gas prices due to structural factors (supply diversification, storage dynamics, LNG flows, and geopolitics) rather than near-term stabilization. The piece emphasizes that without a synchronized global market, episodes of price spikes or divergence across regions may persist through 2027, with potential implications for inflation, energy-intensive sectors, and policy responses.

news.title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Test Support at $3/mmBtu - WSJ
news.summary:
Summary:

- U.S. natural gas futures tested support near $3/mmBtu as production rising and LNG feedgas flows increase. Henry Hub physical prices recently peaked around $3.32/mmBtu due to record Gulf Coast LNG demand and pipeline constraints. Analysts (e.g., EBW Analytics) suggest potential support for the November contract around $3/mmBtu; current Nymex reading near $2.996/mmBtu, down ~2%.

- The near-term mood is mixed: futures are soft, but strong LNG demand and ongoing supply dynamics could cap downside if support holds around $3.

- European prices rise on geopolitical risks, with the Dutch TTF up ~1.7%. While risk factors remain elevated, global LNG supply developments (new non-Qatar capacity) may ease displacement pressure between Europe and Asia, potentially moderating price spikes over the longer term.

Bottom line for a macro outlook: U.S. gas prices appear to be testing a key support zone near $3/mmBtu amid rising shale/gas production and LNG demand; near-term risk remains tied to LNG flows, domestic production, and potential weather/Cushion factors. European prices remain elevated on geopolitical risk but could ease as new LNG capacity affects global supply balance.

news.title: Natural Gas: Volatile winter as Persian Gulf LNG stays scarce – ING
news.summary:
Summary:
- ING’s Warren Patterson notes European natural gas (TTF) prices near their highest since Dec 2022 as Persian Gulf LNG remains scarce, down ~80% year-on-year.
- With Persian Gulf LNG unlikely to recover soon, Asia and Europe will compete for spot cargoes, supporting prices and risk of spikes.
- European gas storage is around 75% full, below the 5-year average (~89%), reinforcing price support; Germany is mandating additional 8 TWh storage by mid-December.
- Mild winter risks exist due to El Niño, but this signal is uncertain and not guaranteed to ease prices.
- ING’s outlook: TTF average ~EUR 73/MWh for the 26/27 winter (up from ~EUR 65/MWh), with high volatility given constrained storage. Prices expected to fall aggressively from 2Q27 as Persian Gulf supply normalizes and US LNG capacity rises.

Takeaway on the macro outlook:
- Structural tightness persists into the 26/27 winter driven by scarce Persian Gulf LNG and low European storage.
- The market faces upside risk from winter weather and ongoing competition for LNG cargoes, with potential for sharp downside as supply normalizes in 2Q27.

news.title: Natural Gas Price Analysis – Warmth Challenges a Mixed Storage Balance | FXEmpire
news.summary:
Natural gas price outlook (macro analysis):

- Price action: Remains range-bound between roughly $3.00 and $3.30 per MMBtu, with recent volatility around the 50-day EMA but no clear breakout.
- Storage context: October storage data show a modest seasonal surplus (~45 Bcf above five-year average) but still well below last year’s level, implying a mixed supply picture rather than an outright surplus or shortage.
- Demand drivers:
  - Heating demand potential: NOAA/PC forecasts suggest above-normal temperatures in much of the East and cooler trends in parts of the West, which could temper near-term heating demand and limit upside.
  - Exports: U.S. LNG and pipeline exports are rising but remain a factor rather than the dominant driver; actual impact depends on whether export capacity materially draws gas from storage.
- Weather risk: The macro case hinges on weather revisions. Warmer-than-normalOctober outlooks reduce near-term urgency to secure winter gas; colder revisions or stronger export demand could shift the balance.
- Outlook takeaways:
  - The market looks to be in a consolidation zone (roughly $3.00–$3.30) with no clear directional bias.
  - Short-term moves will largely hinge on weather updates and the next EIA storage report, rather than a wholesale supply surplus.
  - If warmer forecasts persist, expect limited upside and possible dips toward the lower end of the range; if colder signals emerge, a break above $3.30 could be tested.

news.title: Base metals head to LME Week 2026 with record-low TCs, war-hit supply chains - Fastmarkets
news.summary:
Base metals outlook (copper, aluminum, zinc) ahead of LME Week 2026:

- Copper: Prices near record highs entering LME Week. Three-month copper hit intraday highs around $14,875/tonne in Sept 2026 asUS Section 232 tariff risk pulled refined copper into the US, drained LME stocks, and pushed spreads into backwardation. Copper concentrates TC index fell sharply to negative territory (enduring tight concentrate terms). 2027 contract terms expected to be discussed, with 2026 annual benchmark at $0/t and 0 c/lb.

- Zinc: Concentrate TCs collapsed to new lows in 2026 due to tight supply and elevated by-product payables, squeezing smelter economics. Zinc CIF China spot TCs averaged deeply negative near -$115 to -$150/tonne. Outlook hinges on 2027 mine supply growth and winter smelter cuts in northern China; El Niño disruptions could further weigh on zinc concentrate shipments and inputs.

- Aluminum: Europe’s primary aluminum market watch for rising Asian deliveries (Indonesia, India) and resultant impact on European premiums, especially in duty-unpaid markets. Middle East production ramp-ups post-US–Iran conflict could sustain premium pressure in duty-unpaid markets and cap duty-paid premiums. GCC production is expected to reach 75-80% of pre-war levels by early 2027; EGA’s Al Taweelah restart anticipated next year. Aluminium P1020A premium assessed at around $550-585/tonne in Rotterdam (mid-October 2026).

- Risk factors to monitor: El Niño-driven supply disruptions (Nov 2026–Feb 2027), Indonesia’s nickel ore quota management, and geopolitical risks such as strait/disruption impacting sulfuric acid, freight costs, and overall input costs. Tariff dynamics continue to influence copper arbitrage and LME spreads.

Bottom line: Copper remains expensive with tight concentrate terms and tariff-driven demand dynamics; zinc remains under pressure from trough TC levels amid by-product value supports; aluminum premiums face regional shifts due to Asia-to-Europe supply flows and Middle East ramp-ups, all set against weather and geopolitical risk ahead of LME Week 2027 contract term discussions.

news.title: Copper flat as China caution outweighs US stockpiling, Goldman upgrade - Markets - Business Recorder

- Copper prices were flat as cautious Chinese buying at high prices offset Goldman Sachs’ higher forecasts and rising US inventories ahead of possible tariffs.
- Goldman raised its end-2026 copper price forecast to $14,700/ton and 2027 average to $15,400/ton, citing weaker mine supply and firmer markets outside the US; projected deficits outside the US: 950,000 tons (2026) and 220,000 tons (2027).

- Other base metals: aluminum down slightly; zinc and nickel modestly higher; mixed moves across SHFE.
- Notable company news: BHP copper output dropped 19% year-on-year due to disruptions in Chile/Australia, but annual guidance remains unchanged.

news.title: Metals Rebound as Sentiment Improves After Volatile Week
news.summary:

- Metals broadly rebounded after a volatile week, with copper up about 1% to $14,493/ton, aluminum up ~1% to $3,017/ton, and zinc up ~0.9% to $3,697/ton on the London Metal Exchange.

- Near-term outlook mixed: prices likely to stay range-bound amid tight monetary conditions and sector-specific fundamentals.

news.title: Copper price leads base metals higher ahead of LME Week - Mining.com.au

Copper price leads base metals higher ahead of LME Week, with mixed signals for near-term outlook:
- Copper rose 0.3% to $14,384/tonne on the LME, after a brief drop to $14,256, supported by a softer dollar and steadier equity markets.
- Market structure shows nearby copper, zinc, and aluminium in backwardation, signaling tight near-term supply.
- Copper is up about 16% year-to-date; a potential year-end pressure could come as US-bound shipments clear in early December, easing available supply outside the US.
- Aluminium (+0.5%), zinc (+0.7%), nickel (+0.7%), lead (+0.4%), and tin (+0.3%) also moved higher, with specific drivers:
  - Aluminium: expected 2027 surplus due to Indonesian supply and Gulf smelter recoveries.
  - Zinc: Chinese exports rising may weigh on prices.
  - Nickel: higher Indonesian costs provide support despite recent lows.
Overall takeaway: Base metals are firmer ahead of LME Week, with copper leading gains, potential upside near-term supported by tightness in refined copper, but upside may face headwinds from seasonal shipment dynamics and mixed macro signals.
